newsitem.title: FRANCE: Opinion poll puts Juppe's support at new low.
newsitem.headline: Opinion poll puts Juppe's support at new low.

text.p: Support for France's conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who is under fire for austerity policies and high unemployment, has tumbled to a new record low, an opinion poll said on Saturday.

The IFOP survey for the Journal du Dimanche newspaper said only 21 percent of voters were happy with Juppe as premier, down from 27 percent in September. The number of those dissatisfied with him increased to 69 percent from 61.
It was Juppe's worst rating since he took office in May 1995 on a short-lived wave of enthusiasm.
His previous low was 26-65 percent in November 1995 when he was buffeted by controversy over a welfare reform plan that triggered a crippling 24-day wave of strikes.

Civil service labour unions staged a one-day strike last Thursday against feared jobs cuts, record unemployment of 12.6 percent and Juppe's austerity policies aimed at enabling France to qualify for a single European currency from 1999.

President Jacques Chirac fared little better in the poll. It said only 28 percent were satisfied with his performance, down from 31 percent in September, while those unhappy with him rose to 61 percent from 55.
